answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each identity to lock a refundable bond before it can transact, released only after peers attest its work over time. One identity is cheap, but a thousand fake identities mean a thousand locked bonds, so an attacker must tie up capital in proportion to the fakes. If peers prove an identity submitted copied work, its bond is slashed, like a lagoon mistaken for an oasis that drains through karst channels when tested, leaving only identities with real, costly history.
